newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian union threatens strike over benefits.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian union threatens strike over benefits.

text.p: Slovenia's biggest trade union on Tuesday threatened to stage a two-hour general strike on October 24 unless the Associaton of Employers and the Chamber of Economy retracted plans for hefty cuts in social benefits.
"We hope that employers will respect our demands. If they don't, we will be forced to stage a general strike," Dusan Semolic, president of the Association of Free Trade Unions (ZSSS), told Reuters.

Semolic said the ZSSS was not willing to accept cuts in average holiday pay, monthly sick pay, strike compensation pay, redundancy pay and daily allowances that were suggested by employers earlier this month.
Employers and the Chamber of Economy proposed the cuts in a bid to cut the country's ballooning wage costs and improve the economy's competitiveness.

Slovenia was hit by a wave of pay strikes over the summer and the government had to give in to many demands. Analysts have warned that unrestrained growth in Slovenian wages could fuel inflation and endanger economic stability.
The average gross monthly salary in Slovenia was 131,315 tolars ($951) in August, up 17.2 percent from a year earlier.
